You don't need the $100 Gemini plan this week. The most-watched review of Gemini 4 Carbon calls it "slow, awkward, stupid". Run 3 prompts on the free model first. If it passes, keep your $100.

What happened: Google shipped Gemini 4 Carbon on Monday. It only comes with the Ultra plan ($100 a month) and the API, where the price doubles on December 1. The first big review, 247,000 views, says it hallucinates a lot but has useful things "hidden deep".

So here is a simple rule. A new model has to fail at your work on the old model before you pay for it. Not fail a benchmark. Fail your task.

These 3 tests take 20 minutes on free Argon. Paste your own material into each one.

Test 1: Find the trap
"Here is a long document. One number or date inside it contradicts another part of the same document. Find it, quote both places, and explain which one is probably right and why. If you find no contradiction, say so. Do not invent one."

Test 2: Plan without guessing
"Make a 6-step plan to [your task]. After every step, write one line: what fact this step depends on, and whether you know it or are guessing. Stop at the first step where you are guessing and ask me."

Test 3: Fix one bug, break nothing
"This code has exactly one bug. Find it, fix only that line, and list every other line you were tempted to change but did not. Then write the one test that would have caught the bug."

Score each test: found it, missed it, or made something up. If Argon gets 3 out of 3, the $100 model is solving a problem you do not have. If it fails one, you now know exactly what you are paying Carbon to do.

You can leave your next call with the doc already written. Not notes. The doc, with owners and dates.

Anthropic shipped this last night. 14,000 bookmarks in 12 hours. Team plans only.

Two prompts below get you the same thing on the $20 plan, and the second one works on last week's calls too. Here's how.

What it does: Claude joins your Google Meet as a participant. You talk, it builds the doc or the whiteboard live, and everyone on the call sees it and corrects it. After the call, the notes, action items and transcript sit on the meeting's page. Beta, Team and Enterprise only, Meet first.

Here is the part the launch video skips. An AI in the call changes nothing if nobody says what has to exist when the call ends. Most meetings end with "let's sync next week" because nobody named the output. Name it in the first minute and the meeting gets shorter, with or without Claude in it.

Prompt 1: Before the call (paste into Claude Meetings, or read it out loud to your team)
"This call has one output: [a one-page decision doc / a launch checklist / a priced proposal]. Build it as we talk. Mark something as a decision only after its owner says yes out loud. Keep a list of open questions with a name next to each one. If we drift for more than 3 minutes, say so. Five minutes before the end, read back every decision and its owner."

Prompt 2: After the call (any plan: Google Meet records the transcript for you, paste it)
"Here is the transcript. Give me: 1) every decision, with the line where it was agreed, 2) owners and due dates, writing [unassigned] where none was given, 3) open questions, 4) anything that sounded like a decision but nobody confirmed, 5) a 5-line follow-up email. Do not invent an owner or a date."

Run prompt 2 on last week's meeting. If you find three decisions nobody owns, that is your Monday.

Bad meetings all have the same bug. Nothing was due when they ended.
